requirements.evidence: All contract routes are in routes/web.php:18-43 with the right names, methods and middleware: guest group, throttle:6,1 on password.email, signed+throttle on verification.verify, and verified on home. Login (app/Livewire/Auth/Login.php:18-70) uses email:rfc,strict, throws auth.failed on email, keys the limiter on Str::lower(email)|ip with 5 tries, throws auth.throttle when locked, calls session()->regenerate() and redirectIntended(route('home')). Register (app/Livewire/Auth/Register.php:35-80) uses the exact str()->transliterate('register|'.ip) key, Password::defaults(), unique and confirmed, fires Registered, logs in and regenerates. Logout (LogoutController.php:16-21) invalidates the session and regenerates the token. PasswordResetController.php:29-82 always flashes passwords.sent and rotates remember_token with Str::random(60) before firing PasswordReset. The reset view has a single name="email" input. User implements MustVerifyEmail. EmailVerificationRequest gives 403 for tampered ids, and resend skips verified users (EmailVerificationController.php:40-42). Locale pins are in .env.example and phpunit.xml, and ui.php exists in both locales. Existing views are not in the diff, so their compliance with the href rule is covered only by the new ViewConventionsTest.

conventions.evidence: Livewire components use #[Validate] and $this->validate(). Reusable markup is extracted into anonymous Blade components (components/field.blade.php, auth/card.blade.php, status.blade.php). Bulma classes are used throughout, User keeps #[Fillable], controllers use inline $request->validate, and CHANGELOG and docs/business-rules.md are updated. Deviations: Register mixes #[Validate] for name with a rules() method for email and password (Register.php:22 vs 74-80), and the user-creation write is done inline with User::create in the component rather than through an app/Actions class.

security.evidence: Rate limiting is server-side in both Livewire actions. RedirectIfAuthenticated is registered as persistent middleware (AppServiceProvider.php:37), so logged-in users cannot call Login or Register update endpoints. Forgot password does not enumerate accounts, and an InvalidUser reset is mapped to InvalidToken (PasswordResetController.php:76-78). remember_token is rotated on reset, session regeneration and invalidation are in place, all output uses {{ }}, and verification relies on EmailVerificationRequest. Minor gap: layouts/app.blade.php:13 falls back to a third-party CDN stylesheet (cdn.jsdelivr.net) with no integrity attribute.

tests.evidence: There are thorough Pest feature tests for every flow: LoginTest (lockout per lowercase e-mail, intended redirect, limiter clear), RegisterTest (confirmed rule, default password rule, IP limit, unique case-insensitive), PasswordResetTest (7th request returns 429, single email input, remember token rotation), EmailVerificationTest (tampered id 403, wrong hash, unsigned, throttle, resend), plus HomeAccessTest, LocalizationTest and ViewConventionsTest. Weak spots: the 'remember me' test (LoginTest.php:55-66) only checks that getRememberToken() is not empty, and the factory already sets a remember_token, so the test cannot fail. The persistent-middleware test only asserts registration and never makes an authenticated Livewire call to submit().

simplicity.evidence: Lean controllers, framework-native EmailVerificationRequest, Password broker and RateLimiter, and a small x-field component reused across all forms. The Vite-or-CDN branch in layouts/app.blade.php:10-14 is unnecessary indirection.

readability.evidence: Small focused methods with PHPDoc (e.g. PasswordResetController::email, Login::ensureIsNotRateLimited). Comments explain non-obvious security choices (Register.php:45-46, AppServiceProvider.php:35-36), naming is clear, and there is no dead code. Only nit: Login::submit and Register::submit have no return type.

scope.evidence: Nearly everything serves the task. There are a few unrelated edits: bootstrap/providers.php is rewritten to use imports, trailing newlines and a quote style are changed in lang/pt_BR/{auth,pagination,passwords,validation}.php, and an unused import is removed from tests/Feature/BulmaTest.php. These are Pint-style cleanups, harmless but not asked for.

issues.explanation: The remember-me test only checks that the remember token is not empty, but the default factory already sets a remember_token, so the test passes even if 'remember' is ignored; it should assert the recaller cookie or that the token changed.

The Livewire policy asks for an unauthorized-call test per action, but the test only checks the persistent middleware list; there is no test of an authenticated user calling Login/Register submit() directly.

When there is no Vite build, the layout loads Bulma from a third-party CDN without Subresource Integrity, which adds an external dependency and supply-chain exposure the project's Vite setup does not need.
Validation is split between a #[Validate] attribute (name) and a rules() method (email, password) in the same component, which is inconsistent with the project's #[Validate] pattern.
The user-creation write is done inline in the component instead of through an app/Actions class, as the 'domain writes go through Actions' convention suggests.
The registration lockout reuses auth.throttle, which in pt_BR says 'Muitas tentativas de login', a slightly misleading message on the sign-up form.
These are unrelated style-only edits (import rewrites, trailing newlines, quote style, removed unused import) that are not part of the task.
submit() has no return type, unlike the other methods in the change.

review.summary: The change builds the full session-auth flow: Livewire login and register, logout, forgot and reset password, and e-mail verification. It ships pt_BR-first translations, a Bulma layout and Blade components, docs and changelog updates, and an extensive Pest suite. Requirements and security hardening (rate limits, no enumeration, remember-token rotation, persistent guest middleware) are well covered. Remaining points are minor: one weak remember-me test, no unauthorized Livewire call test, a CDN fallback without SRI, mixed validation styles and a few unrelated style edits, so I would approve with nits.
